o: Heavenly Father, I thank You for this new day You have set before me. Before the rush and the worries begin, I want to pause for a moment and acknowledge that You are my Lord, my refuge and my strength. You kept me through the night and woke me with life and hope. Everything I have comes from Your generous hand.

Today, Lord, contrary winds may blow: news I did not expect, tasks that weigh on me and situations that make me doubt. I confess that sometimes I fill with fear and it seems the boat is sinking. But You are not far from me. Teach me to trust You when the sea is stirred, and to remember that a single word from You is enough to bring calm. Take from my heart the fear that paralyzes and give me a simple and firm faith.

Guide my steps, my words and my decisions throughout this day. May I speak with kindness, work with diligence and rest in Your care. When I feel weak, remind me that You are with me in the same boat. Fill my home with peace and protect the people I love. I give You this whole day, with everything it will bring, trusting that You will do what is best. In Jesus' name, amen.
h: That evening, on the shore of the Sea of Galilee, Jesus had served many people and he was tired. So he gave his disciples a simple command: let us go over to the other side of the lake. They got into the boat with him and set sail. Among them were fishermen who knew these waters well, and nothing suggested the trip would be difficult.

Suddenly, a storm so fierce arose on the sea that the waves were covering the boat. These men, used to the lake, were seized with fear. Meanwhile, Jesus was asleep. He was neither absent nor indifferent; he was exhausted, and he was with them in the same boat. In desperation, they woke him and said: Lord, save us, we are perishing!

Jesus answered them: Why are you afraid, you of little faith? Then he rose, rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm. The disciples were amazed and said to one another: What kind of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him? This scene is found in chapter 8 of the Gospel of Matthew.

Notice a very important detail: the storm came while the disciples were obeying Jesus. Being on God's path does not spare us from storms, but it assures us that the Master goes with us. The disciples had to learn that the presence of Jesus in the boat is greater than any wave. They also learned that crying out to him, even with little faith, is never in vain. He listens, rises and acts at the right moment, and his voice has authority over everything that seems impossible for us to master.
m.c: Today, may you walk with the certainty that Jesus is with you in the boat. When the strong wind comes, remember that his word brings calm. Go out with peace and courage, for the Lord cares for you at every hour.
m: Fear is one of the most human emotions. The disciples felt it even though they were with Jesus, and we feel it too. It can come in the form of worry about health, work, family or the future. The good news is that the Bible does not reproach us for being afraid; it teaches us what to do with it. The psalmist David wrote: When I am afraid, I put my trust in you. Notice that he does not say he would never be afraid, but that he decided to trust.

Trust begins when we bring our fear to Jesus, as the disciples did. They woke him and told him the truth: we are perishing. We do not need to pretend to be strong before God. We can say to him sincerely: Lord, I am afraid, help me. He does not mock our weakness; on the contrary, he draws near. And although Jesus pointed out their little faith, he did not abandon them. He gave them calm and showed them who he was.

For today, I propose something practical. Think of the situation that worries you most and put it into a short prayer, in your own words. Then read Psalm 56, verses 3 and 4, aloud, and slowly repeat: In God I trust; I shall not be afraid. If fear returns during the day, repeat that phrase. Breathing deeply and remembering God's word is a simple way to hand him the burden again and again.

Seek also to be a person who brings calm to others. Perhaps someone around you is going through a storm of their own. A kind word, a call or a moment of listening can be like a small ray of peace. Jesus calmed the sea with a word, and he sends us to be bearers of his peace. Go out today with the assurance that you are not sailing alone: the one who commands the winds is with you in the boat.

o: Lord and my Father, at the end of this day, I come before You with a grateful heart. Thank You for the air I breathed, for daily bread and for the people with whom I shared these hours. Thank You, because even in the hard moments, Your hand did not let go of me. I acknowledge that everything good in this day came from You.

I confess, Lord, that today too there was weariness. There were moments when I felt without strength, wanting to give up, with the weight of things I could not settle. Now I place in Your hands the burdens I carried all day: the worries, the mistakes, the words I did not know how to say and the tasks left pending. I do not want to take them to bed with me. You know how to take care of me better than I know how to do it myself.

Give me, Father, true rest tonight. May my body be renewed and my mind be calmed. Take care of my family and of all those I love, and keep also those who are alone, sick or discouraged today. May I be able to rise tomorrow with new strength, knowing that You feed me and accompany me on the way. I lie down in peace, for You make me dwell in safety. In Jesus' name, amen.
h: The prophet Elijah had lived extraordinary days. He had seen God's power on Mount Carmel, and the people had cried out that the LORD was the true God. But soon after, Queen Jezebel swore to take his life. Elijah, who had been so courageous, became afraid and fled. He came to Beersheba, left his servant there and went on alone, a day's journey into the wilderness.

Exhausted and discouraged, he sat down under a broom tree and asked God to take his life. He said: It is enough! O LORD, take my life, for I am no better than my fathers. Then he lay down and fell asleep. He was a faithful man who had reached the end of his strength. God did not take him up on it and did not leave him alone with his sadness.

An angel touched him and said: Get up and eat. Elijah looked, and there by his head was a cake baked on hot stones and a jar of water. He ate and drank and lay down again. The angel came a second time, touched him and said: Get up and eat, for the journey is too great for you. This is how chapter 19 of the first book of Kings tells it.

Elijah got up, ate and drank, and in the strength of that food he walked forty days and forty nights to Horeb, the mountain of God. Observe how God first took care of his tired body, through rest and food, before speaking to his heart. Sometimes what we need most at the end of a hard day is to sleep, to eat something and to know that the Lord continues to watch. He knows our limits and does not ask more of us than what we can give in a day.
t.c: As you close this day, give the Lord everything that has weighed on your shoulders. He takes care of you while you sleep and renews your strength for the road ahead. Rest easy, for his love covers you all night long.
m: We often think that faith means being always strong and full of energy. Yet the Bible shows us a great prophet like Elijah, sitting under a tree, exhausted and with no desire to go on. This teaches us that deep weariness is not a sign of lack of faith. God's servants also grow tired, get discouraged and need to be lifted up. If you end today's journey this way, do not feel guilty: you are in good company.

Notice how the Lord responded. He did not give Elijah a long speech or a list of reproaches. He sent him rest, food and water, and a gentle touch that said: get up. God knows that we are dust and he responds to our real needs. When you are exhausted, caring for your body, sleeping enough and eating calmly is also a way of letting God sustain you.

King David wrote: Cast your burden on the LORD, and he will sustain you; he will never permit the righteous to be moved. To cast your burden means to let it go for real. Tonight, before sleeping, you can do a simple exercise: name each worry in prayer and say in a low voice: Lord, this I give to you. If you remember something else during the night, repeat it. You do not have to settle everything today.

And tomorrow, the same God who strengthened Elijah for a long journey will give you strength for yours. We will not always see the end of the road all at once, but we will have the food needed for each stage. Trust that the Lord will lift you up in his time. Sleep in peace: the one who keeps you neither slumbers nor sleeps, and his faithfulness does not fail.
